question: 11 Member States have called for a 12-month pause on new EU legislation, in what they are calling a ‘year of simplification’. Their message is straightforward: Brussels cannot keep piling new rules on citizens, businesses and national administrations while existing legislation is still being implemented, reviewed and enforced.

The Commission has repeatedly promised ‘better regulation’ and simplification, yet the flow of new legislation has continued. This raises the more fundamental question of whether the problem is not simply excessive red tape, but a Commission culture of regulatory overreach. 1.
What assessment has the Commission made of the proposal for a year of simplification by this blocking minority in the Council?

Does the Commission recognise that the sheer volume and cumulative effect of EU legislation has itself become a problem, and is it prepared to conduct an honest selfreflection on its own role in creating regulatory overreach, including by identifying areas where it has proposed legislation without a sufficiently demonstrated need for action at EU level?

Which legislative proposals currently under preparation does the Commission consider unnecessary, duplicative or suitable for postponement or withdrawal, and will it commit to putting them on hold during a year of simplification?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.11.2026) The Commission took note of the non-paper by 11 Member States calling for a stronger focus on the efficient implementation of existing legislation. The Commission is aware that regulatory fragmentation poses an important challenge for companies and public administrations.

In April 2026, it outlined an Action Plan for regulatory deep cleaning with 12 priority areas for 2026 and 2027, and remains committed to stress testing the whole EU acquis by the end of its mandate in 2029. The Commission has also outlined key principles of simplicity by design and regulatory discipline to inform any new proposals1.

Increasing the coherence and consistency of EU legislation, including by consolidating existing legal acts, are important objectives. At the same time, not every legal act adds burden. Omnibus and simplification proposals, reduce burdens for businesses, citizens and administrations and/or directly contribute to improve competitiveness.

The Commission is fully engaged in a thorough simplification throughout this mandate with the objective to reduce burdens for companies and small and medium-sized enterprises. So far, the Commission has proposed measures that have the potential to achieve 60% of the target to cut administrative costs by EUR 37.

5 billion by the end of this mandate, if their level of ambition is preserved by the European Parliament and the Council during the legislative process. The 2027 work programme also has a strong emphasis on delivery, implementation and enforcement on key priorities, including competitiveness and simplification; it also contains a list of 18 proposed legislative initiatives to withdraw and 14 envisaged repeals.
